prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1246; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The claimant's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claim was assigned for review the same day.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of loss. No issues with the policy have been identified.

Entry 3: Reviewed the first set of photos from the scene. They show the rear bumper and trunk area of the claimant's vehicle, consistent with the described impact. Independent witnesses were not identified.

Entry 4: Recorded the claimant's account by phone. The claimant described the collision and reported a shoulder injury, and the account matched the original report in its main points.

Entry 5: Requested prior claims history for the vehicle. No earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 6: Obtained the repair estimate. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, with the rear panel and bumper as the primary areas affected.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical records provided through counsel. The shoulder injury fits the kind and force of the collision well, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known.

Entry 8: Spoke with claimant's counsel, who confirmed representation and asked that all contact go through their office. Counsel provided the claimant's account, which matches what the claimant told us in earlier conversations.

Entry 9: Noted that the file does not make clear where in the vehicle the claimant was seated at impact. Counsel was asked to clarify, and a follow-up request was sent.

Entry 10: Reviewed treatment records. Care followed a usual course and tapered as the claimant improved, with no unusual gaps or escalations noted.

Entry 11: Summarized the file for supervisor review. Liability and damage details are consistent with the reported loss, and the seating position question is the only open item pending counsel's response.
